claim: Kitson and Constantinou, arXiv 2608.27472, Aug 2026
work: Neville K. Kitson, Anthony Constantinou, 'LLM-Augmented Causal Discovery: Probabilistic Fusion of Edge Existence and Orientation', arXiv 2608.27472
quote: none
correction: Authors, ID and date correct (v1 only, 19 Aug 2026).

claim: LLM better at orientation than at existence
work: Kitson and Constantinou, arXiv 2608.27472
quote: "LLM achieves a mean orientation accuracy of 0.96"
correction: Holds; more precise: LLM orientation accuracy 0.96 vs structure learning 0.77; LLM edge recall 0.603 vs 0.802 for structure learning.

claim: Source is lost after fusion
work: Kitson and Constantinou, arXiv 2608.27472
quote: "merge the BNSL and LLM ensemble PDGs into one fused PDG"
correction: Follows from the method (single weighted average per pair); the paper does not say it in these words, so phrase as a consequence of the design.

claim: No circle or bidirected state
work: Kitson and Constantinou, arXiv 2608.27472
quote: "lacks an explicit bidirected edge state"
correction: Four states only (absent, forward, backward, undirected); no PAG marks.

claim: No abstention
work: Kitson and Constantinou, arXiv 2608.27472
quote: "ONLY include edges with existence >= 0.5"
correction: No abstention or 'unknown' mechanism described; only an existence filter in the prompt.

claim: Li and Russo, arXiv 2602.16481
work: Zihao Li, Fabrizio Russo, 'Leveraging Large Language Models for Causal Discovery: a Constraint-based, Argumentation-driven Approach', arXiv 2602.16481; PMLR v337 (li26e)
quote: none
correction: Authors and ID correct. arXiv page carries no venue; PMLR v337 entry li26e exists (search result). Cite v2.

claim: LLM constraints kept only if five queries agree
work: Li and Russo, arXiv 2602.16481v2
quote: "We query the primary LLM five times independently with the same prompt."
correction: Kept only if unanimous across the five answers.

claim: LLM constraints entered as defeasible assumptions
work: Li and Russo, arXiv 2602.16481v2
quote: "is treated as a hard directional fact,"
correction: In the current implementation a consensus LLM direction is a hard directional fact, enforced only if its adjacency survives CI-based skeleton reduction. Making LLM constraints defeasible (calibrated against CI-test confidence) is stated as future work.

claim: Required arrow dropped if strong data evidence removed that adjacency
work: Li and Russo, arXiv 2602.16481v2
quote: "an LLM orientation can be blocked when the corresponding adjacency has been removed"
correction: Drop 'strong': the arrow is blocked whenever a CI test removed the adjacency; no evidence-strength threshold. LLM input can orient surviving edges but cannot add edges.

claim: DAGs only, about 15 nodes
work: Li and Russo, arXiv 2602.16481v2
quote: "number of nodes |V| in {5, 10, 15}"
correction: DAG output confirmed. Synthetic graphs have 5-15 nodes, but benchmarks go up to CHILD (20 nodes). Say 'DAGs only, 5-20 nodes'.

claim: No confidence on individual LLM statements
work: Li and Russo, arXiv 2602.16481v2
quote: "they would need to be calibrated against CI-test confidence"
correction: LLM constraints are binary after unanimity; confidence ranking applies to CI facts only.

claim: Memorisation-resistant benchmark: random graphs mapped onto CauseNet; meaningful names on unseen graphs
work: Li and Russo, arXiv 2602.16481v2
quote: "embeds randomly generated DAG structures within CauseNet"
correction: Add caveat: authors do not claim individual CauseNet relations are unseen by the LLM; the graph structure is new, not the edges.

location: pass6_literature_map.md s2 LLMs as imperfect experts
claim: Kiciman et al. (2305.00050): strong pairwise accuracy and partial memorisation of the benchmark
work: Emre Kiciman, Robert Ness, Amit Sharma, Chenhao Tan, 'Causal Reasoning and Large Language Models: Opening a New Frontier for Causality', arXiv 2305.00050v3
section: Abstract; s3.1 Table 2; s3.3 Memorization Test Results
quote: "certainly in GPT's training set"
correction: 97% on Tuebingen pairs (GPT-4); GPT-4 recalled 25% of Tuebingen rows (GPT-3.5 19%). Authors argue capability is not explained by memorisation alone.

location: pass6_literature_map.md s2 LLMs as imperfect experts
claim: Long et al. (2307.02390): the only guarantee 'true graph stays in returned class with prob >= 1-eta', under a constant-error expert model
work: Stephanie Long, Alexandre Piche, Valentina Zantedeschi, Tibor Schuster, Alexandre Drouin, 'Causal Discovery with Language Models as Imperfect Experts', arXiv 2307.02390v1
quote: "is incorrect with constant probability"
correction: Guarantee and epsilon-expert model confirmed, but the bound is a posterior estimate that holds only if the epsilon-expert model is right. 'The only guarantee of this form' is a claim about our search, not the paper: write 'the clearest guarantee of this form we found'.

location: pass6_literature_map.md s2 LLMs as imperfect experts
claim: Long et al.: their own LLM test broke it through over-confidence
work: Long et al., arXiv 2307.02390v1
quote: "The text-davinci-003 model is often over-confident in its answers"
correction: Partly. Over-confidence is the stated cause for text-davinci-003; on ALARM, G* was excluded because of 'ambiguities in the metadata'. Say: 'their LLM test violated it, through over-confidence and ambiguous metadata'.

location: pass6_literature_map.md s2 LLMs as imperfect experts

work: Aniket Vashishtha, Abbavaram Gowtham Reddy, Abhinav Kumar, Saketh Bachu, Vineeth N Balasubramanian, Amit Sharma, 'Causal Order: The Key to Leveraging Imperfect Experts in Causal Inference', arXiv 2310.15117v2

work: Taiyu Ban, Lyuzhou Chen, Derui Lyu, Xiangyu Wang, Huanhuan Chen, 'Causal Structure Learning Supervised by Large Language Model', arXiv 2311.11689v1
quote: "focuses LLMs on verifying direct causal relationships already suggested by the data"
correction: Verdicts become hard or soft constraints for the next structure-learning round (iterative).

correction: They still allow a supporting role (e.g. LLM-guided heuristic search).

work: Tao Feng, Lizhen Qu, Niket Tandon, Zhuang Li, Xiaoxi Kang, Gholamreza Haffari, 'On the Reliability of Large Language Models for Causal Discovery', arXiv 2407.19638v2
quote: "effective in recognizing causal relations that occur frequently in pre-training data"
correction: Qualitative in the abstract; v2 dated 10 Oct 2025.

claim: DMCD (2602.20333) uses neutral names as a control
work: Samarth KaPatel, Sofia Nikiforova, Giacinto Paolo Saggese, Paul Smith, 'DMCD: Semantic-Statistical Framework for Causal Discovery', arXiv 2602.20333v1
quote: "renamed all variables to neutral identifiers"

claim: CausalDS (2607.08093): name swaps holding data fixed
work: Andrej Leban, Yuekai Sun, 'CausalDS: Benchmarking Causal Reasoning in Data-Science Agents', arXiv 2607.08093v1
quote: "answers do not hinge on the particular pairs seeded"
correction: It is a matched verbalization-swap ablation: the seeded story and variable names change while graph, SCM and data stay fixed. Not a swap of names between variables. Say 'story/name re-verbalization holding data fixed'.

claim: Han et al. (2408.06849): random-word names
work: Kairong Han, Kun Kuang, Ziyu Zhao, Junjian Ye, Fei Wu, 'Causal Agent based on Large Language Model', arXiv 2408.06849v3
quote: "the keywords that come from the list are randomly drawn"
correction: Variables are real-word keywords drawn at random (possibly causally unrelated) so the agent must rely on the data; the paper does not frame this as a memorisation control. Say 'randomly drawn keyword names'.

claim: Clivio et al. (2502.13132): learning to defer per pair, two variables only
work: Oscar Clivio, Divyat Mahajan, Perouz Taslakian, Sara Magliacane, Ioannis Mitliagkas, Valentina Zantedeschi, Alexandre Drouin, 'Learning to Defer for Causal Discovery with Imperfect Experts', arXiv 2502.13132v1
quote: "for pairwise causal discovery"
correction: Evaluated on Tuebingen pairs; an extension to larger graphs is only outlined.

claim: Tench and Demeester (2601.16715): selective querying where algorithms disagree (listed among LLM methods)
work: Adrick Tench, Thomas Demeester, 'Dynamic Expert-Guided Model Averaging for Causal Discovery', arXiv 2601.16715v2
quote: "We use a simulated expert in our experiments."
correction: Disagreement-driven querying confirmed, but the expert in the experiments is simulated, not an LLM. Add 'with a simulated expert'.

claim: CauTion (2606.03602): selective querying where algorithms disagree; trust estimation
work: Bo Peng, Kaiwen Wu, Sirui Chen, Zhiheng Wang, Yu Qiao, Chaochao Lu, 'CauTion: Knowing When to Trust LLMs for Ensemble Causal Discovery', arXiv 2606.03602v1
quote: "restricts LLM arbitration exclusively to edges with unreliable algorithmic evidence"
correction: Trust via 'annotation-free trust calibration'; no explicit abstention.

claim: Causal Ensemble Agent (2606.10607) has a with/without-LLM ablation
work: Xinyu Li, Yuanyuan Wang, Haoxuan Li, Chuan Zhou, Erdun Gao, Bo Han, Tongliang Liu, Kun Zhang, Howard Bondell, Mingming Gong, 'Causal Ensemble Agent: Hierarchical Causal Discovery with LLM-guided Expert Reweighting', arXiv 2606.10607v1
quote: "consistently degrades CEA's performance across all datasets"
correction: LLM is triggered by pooled support near the threshold (margin rule) rather than a raw disagreement count.

claim: MosaCD (2509.23570) filters LLM orientations against the data (2025)

quote: "We discard any proposed seed X -> Y that (i) contradicts"
correction: Seeds conflicting with CI-derived separating sets or creating cycles are discarded; also a shuffled-query consistency filter. Date 28 Sep 2025.

claim: Takayama et al. (2402.01454): three-zone thresholds with an explicit unknown band
work: Masayuki Takayama, Tadahisa Okuda, Thong Pham, Tatsuyoshi Ikenoue, Shingo Fukuma, Shohei Shimizu, Akiyoshi Sannai, 'Integrating Large Language Models in Causal Discovery: A Statistical Causal Approach', arXiv 2402.01454v5
quote: "alpha1 is fixed at 0.05, and alpha2 is fixed at 0.95"
correction: Forbidden below 0.05, Forced at or above 0.95, Unknown otherwise; probabilities averaged over M=5 runs.

claim: Friedman, Goldszmidt, Wyner (UAI 1999) treat directed and undirected edges as separate bootstrap features
work: Nir Friedman, Moises Goldszmidt, Abraham Wyner, 'Data Analysis with Bayesian Networks: A Bootstrap Approach', arXiv 1301.6695 (UAI 1999)

claim: bnlearn boot.strength: strength regardless of direction, direction given presence, thresholds strength only (Scutari and Nagarajan 2013)
work: bnlearn documentation, arc.strength / boot.strength; Scutari and Nagarajan, Artif. Intell. Med. 57(3):207-217, 2013
quote: "conditional on the arc being present in the graph (in either direction)"
correction: Averaged network keeps arcs 'whose strength is greater than the threshold'; Scutari and Nagarajan cited for the threshold.

claim: Debeire et al. (CLeaR 2024) vote over edge types with conservative tie-breaking
work: Kevin Debeire, Andreas Gerhardus, Jakob Runge, Veronika Eyring, 'Bootstrap aggregation and confidence measures to improve time series causal discovery', CLeaR 2024, PMLR 236:979-1007 (arXiv 2306.08946)
section: s3.3 Aggregation by edge-wise majority vote
quote: "it prefers edge types that convey less conclusive claims"
correction: Venue confirmed (PMLR 236). Author order differs between arXiv and PMLR.

claim: Jabbari et al. (1712.08626): PAG edge-type frequencies need calibration
work: Fattaneh Jabbari, Mahdi Pakdaman Naeini, Gregory F. Cooper, 'Obtaining Accurate Probabilistic Causal Inference by Post-Processing Calibration', arXiv 1712.08626v1
quote: "These bootstrap estimates are not guaranteed to represent calibrated posterior probabilities"
correction: Bootstrap RFCI (200 resamples); calibration generally improves them.

claim: Kummerfeld and Rix (1910.02047) find bootstrap frequencies persistently miscalibrated
work: Erich Kummerfeld, Alexander Rix, 'Simulations evaluating resampling methods for causal discovery: ensemble performance and calibration', arXiv 1910.02047v1
quote: "performed surprisingly well"
correction: Wrong as stated. They found resampling frequencies good confidence indicators overall; calibration depended on the model (well calibrated for linear Gaussian, poorer on Child, often over-estimating). Remove from 'persistently miscalibrated'; cite only Banerjee et al. for that.

claim: Banerjee et al. (2503.15436) find bootstrap frequencies persistently miscalibrated
work: Ritwick Banerjee, Bryan Andrews, Erich Kummerfeld, 'An extensive simulation study evaluating the interaction of resampling techniques across multiple causal discovery contexts', arXiv 2503.15436v1
quote: "its calibration limitations persist regardless of data abundance"
correction: Applies to the unadjusted bootstrap at the original sample size, in one setting (100 variables, degree 2); other resampling schemes calibrated better.

claim: Error control exists only for adjacency-type selection (Meinshausen and Buhlmann 2010)
work: Nicolai Meinshausen, Peter Buehlmann, 'Stability Selection', JRSS-B 72(4):417-473, 2010 (arXiv 0809.2932)
quote: "provides finite sample control for some error rates of false discoveries"
correction: Stability selection gives this for variable and graphical-model selection. 'Only' is a claim about our search, so say 'the error control we found'.

claim: Meek (1995) for CPDAGs with required and forbidden edges
work: Christopher Meek, 'Causal Inference and Causal Explanation with Background Knowledge', arXiv 1302.4972 (UAI 1995)
quote: "the set of directed edges which are forbidden"
correction: Knowledge K=(F,R) applied to the pattern after adjacencies are fixed.

claim: Perkovic et al. (2017) for CPDAGs with required/forbidden edges
work: Emilija Perkovic, Markus Kalisch, Marloes H. Maathuis, 'Interpreting and using CPDAGs with background knowledge', arXiv 1707.02171v2
quote: "adding background knowledge about certain edge orientations"
correction: Their framing is orientation knowledge giving maximally oriented PDAGs, not 'required and forbidden edges'.

claim: Andrews, Spirtes and Cooper (AISTATS 2020) for FCI with tiered knowledge
work: Bryan Andrews, Peter Spirtes, Gregory F. Cooper, 'On the Completeness of Causal Discovery in the Presence of Latent Confounding with Tiered Background Knowledge', AISTATS 2020, PMLR 108:4002-4011
quote: "show that FCI is sound and complete with the incorporation of this knowledge"

claim: Adding orientation knowledge never deletes an adjacency in these frameworks
work: Meek 1995; Andrews, Spirtes, Cooper 2020
quote: "adjacencies between the members of A are forbidden"
correction: True for Meek (knowledge only orients; inconsistency makes the procedure fail). Andrews et al.'s tiered-knowledge FCI variant also forbids some adjacencies. Say 'orientation-only knowledge never deletes an adjacency; knowledge can forbid adjacencies, but is never silently overridden'.

claim: Weighted constraints solved by ASP (Hyttinen et al. 2014)
work: Antti Hyttinen, Frederick Eberhardt, Matti Jarvisalo, 'Constraint-based Causal Discovery: Conflict Resolution with Answer Set Programming', UAI 2014
quote: "scales to cyclic latent variable models with up to seven observed variables"

work: Sara Magliacane, Tom Claassen, Joris M. Mooij, 'Ancestral Causal Inference', arXiv 1606.07035v3
quote: "otherwise (neither are identifiable)"
correction: Score C(f)=0 when neither feature nor negation is identifiable. Experiments: up to 9 synthetic, 11 real variables.

claim: All stop at roughly 7-15 variables and none exports a per-edge support record
work: Hyttinen 2014; Magliacane 2016; Bromberg and Margaritis 2009; Russo 2024; Li and Russo 2026
quote: "the alarm data set contains 37 variables"
correction: Sizes: Hyttinen 7, ACI 9 (11 real), Russo 2024 10, Li and Russo 20 (CHILD), Bromberg and Margaritis 37 (ALARM). Say 'most stop at 7-20 variables'. ACI does export a per-claim confidence (ancestral, not per edge).

correction: Asia, Cancer, Child, Insurance, Neuropathic, Sachs, Sangiovese; no seeds or variance reported; no renaming control.

claim: MATMCD (2412.13667): gains on famous benchmarks, no renaming control
work: ChengAo Shen, Zhengzhang Chen, Dongsheng Luo, Dongkuan Xu, Haifeng Chen, Jingchao Ni, 'Exploring Multi-Modal Data with Tool-Augmented LLM Agents for Precise Causal Discovery', arXiv 2412.13667v2

claim: MAC (2407.15073): famous benchmarks, mostly single runs, no renaming control

quote: "we run every method over 10 random seeds"
correction: MAC reports mean +/- std over 10 seeds, so it is not a single-run evaluation. No renaming control confirmed (authors flag memorisation as a limitation).

claim: Causal Modelling Agents (ICLR 2024) as a post-hoc LLM refiner; famous benchmarks
work: Ahmed Abdulaal, Adamos Hadjivasiliou, Nina Montana-Brown, Tiantian He, Ayodeji Ijishakin, Ivana Drobnjak, Daniel C. Castro, Daniel C. Alexander, 'Causal Modelling Agents: Causal Graph Discovery through Synergising Metadata- and Data-Driven Reasoning', ICLR 2024
quote: none
correction: Not post-hoc: the LLM proposes the initial graph from metadata and amends it in an iterative loop with a data-driven model. Benchmarks: Arctic sea ice, Sangiovese, synthetic Alzheimer's (not all 'famous'). No renaming control confirmed.

quote: "Method Correctness (F1 score)"

quote: "single-run evaluations misrank models 29.3% of the time"

work: Ke Zhang, Patricio Gallardo Candela, Sudhir Murthy, Yi Xie, Zhi Wang, Maziar Raissi, 'Beyond Compilation: Evaluating Faithful Natural-Language-to-Lean Statement Formalization', arXiv 2606.31002v2

claim: Two-stage pipelines inducing fabricated axioms (Kim et al. 2604.19459)

claim: Formalising hurts on knowledge-heavy tasks (Ganguly et al., NeurIPS 2025)

quote: "from +34.8% on logical tasks to -44.5% on factual ones"
correction: Add the title and arXiv ID; the paper calls these tasks 'factual'.

claim: Kambhampati et al. (ICML 2024): soundness comes only from external critics, and an LLM cannot be the critic
work: Subbarao Kambhampati et al., 'LLMs Can't Plan, But Can Help Planning in LLM-Modulo Frameworks', ICML 2024, PMLR 235 (arXiv 2402.01817)
quote: "cannot take on the role of hard critics with soundness guarantees"
correction: Soundness is inherited from the hard (correctness) critics, which an LLM cannot be; LLMs can act as soft (style) critics and can help write hard critics.
